title: Burst capacity and token-slicing intake - Cedar Ventures
summary: Discovery focused on per-token economics, approaches to bursting reserved capacity, and token-slicing/batching tradeoffs. Customer is evaluating Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private for a mixed low-latency and high-throughput use case and wants a pilot to validate unit costs and SLA behavior.
transcript:
[00:00] Jordan: ok, thanks everyone for joining. we're recording, quick intro — I'm Jordan, AE on the Redwood inference team. Samira's our solutions engineer.
[00:06] Alex: Hey, Alex here, CTO at Cedar Ventures. Thanks, Jordan. We have Priya, Daniel and Meera on from product and infra.
[00:12] Samira: nice to meet you all. quick agenda: understand your workload, cost targets, hosting constraints, and propose a pilot. sound ok?
[00:20] Meera: yes, that's the goal. we want to know how much this will cost when we scale and what tradeoffs we have.
[00:28] Alex: high level, we run a recommendation service and a generative assistant. assistant is low qps, latency sensitive (~100-200ms p50), recommendation is bursty, lots of throughput during batched jobs.
[00:40] Priya: and we have mixed model sizes: 7B for assistant, 33B for ranking/recall. mostly open models but we may try a few third-party hosted ones.
[00:52] Daniel: infra constraint: we need the inference plane within our VPC for certain data. for other workloads we can consider hosted.
[00:58] Jordan: great context. quick clarifying question: when you say bursty, are we talking scheduled nightly jobs or irregular user-driven bursts?
[01:08] Alex: mostly nightly/weekly recall jobs but also periodic traffic spikes during launches. cost is a big factor — we have a monthly budget cap.
[01:15] Samira: ok. on the cost side there are a few levers: per-token pricing (for hosted), reserved capacity pricing (dedicated), batching and KV/prefix caching to reduce per-token compute, and quantization. also routing and fallbacks.
[01:29] Priya: can you explain how batching and the KV cache reduce cost? our understanding is fuzzy.
[01:36] Samira: sure. batching increases GPU utilization — more tokens processed per GPU-second. for seq generation, continuous batching groups requests and amortizes overhead. KV or prefix caching avoids recomputing earlier layers for similar prefixes — so if many queries share context, token cost drops because you only compute the new tokens.
[01:51] Daniel: spelling? is that K V cache or K V K V?
[01:54] Samira: yeah, sorry, KV cache — key/value cache. sometimes transcribed as K V.
[01:58] Alex: do you have typical delta numbers — like what percent cost reduction we could expect?
[02:03] Samira: it depends. for a heavy prefix reuse workload, we've seen 30-70% token compute reduction; for pure batching with short sequences maybe 20-40% improvement. quantization can give another 20-40% depending on model. but numbers vary a lot by distribution.
[02:19] Priya: and for hosted per-token pricing, is that purely per output token or includes input tokens too?
[02:25] Jordan: we bill on both input+output tokens for generation. embeddings are per-unit. we'll send the exact pricing sheet but base is per-token.
[02:33] Meera: what's the math for dedicated? how do we think about unit cost there?
[02:38] Samira: dedicated is reserved GPU capacity — you commit to N GPUs for a period and you get predictable throughput. unit economics are a function of utilization. if you hit high utilization, effective per-token cost is lower than hosted. but you pay for idle capacity when utilization is low. we help with autoscaling policies and burst pools for short spikes.
[02:57] Daniel: burst pools — is that the same as on-demand bursting from hosted?
[03:01] Samira: conceptually yes, but implemented differently. with Redwood Dedicated you can have a reserved pool plus a burst pool that can be on-demand within the same tenant; with Private you can configure similar behavior but depends on your on-prem infra. Hosted bursting is simpler — route overflow to hosted models, but data residency and PII concerns come up.
[03:17] Alex: hmm. we need VPC for the assistant (PHI-ish), but ranking can be hosted. is a split hosting approach common?
[03:24] Jordan: very common. customers pin sensitive workloads to Dedicated or Private and keep batch or non-sensitive to Hosted. routing policies can pick by label.
[03:32] Priya: how does fallback work? if dedicated is saturated does it automatically go to hosted?
[03:36] Samira: yes, you can configure a fallback policy. two things to watch: model parity (you should have a compatible variant in hosted) and cost differences. fallback also preserves api semantics.
[03:45] Alex: about the budget — we have a cap of $75k/mo for inference initially. how do we size a pilot to validate within that?
[03:52] Jordan: usually we run a targeted pilot: pick representative traffic slices and run bench tests to measure tokens/sec and latency across modes. Samira can sketch a micro-benchmark that mimics your nightly recall plus a 10% traffic spike. we then extrapolate.
[04:06] Samira: yeah I can run two experiments: 1) latency-sensitive assistant (single-user conns) to measure p50/p95 on 7B with low batching, 2) batch recall throughput on 33B with large batching and KV cache turned on/off.
[04:19] Priya: how long to get results?
[04:22] Samira: I can run lab runs in a couple days, give preliminary numbers in 5 business days with artifacts (logs, token counts). if we need private infra tests it may take longer for on-prem setup.
[04:34] Daniel: what about SLOs — p50 150ms target — can Redwood meet that on hosted?
[04:40] Samira: for 7B models yes for p50 in many regions but it depends on sequence length and functions like tool-calling/streaming. we have verified profiles per model/region. we can run an exact test with your prompt set.
[04:52] Alex: can you quantify per-token hosted price ballpark? earlier calls mentioned ranges but we need an idea quickly.
[04:58] Jordan: ballpark — depends on model and quantization. for a 7B generation model hosted, think $0.0003–0.001 per 1k tokens depending on SLA and plan. for larger models like 33B it's higher — maybe 3x–6x. again, we'll send the pricing spreadsheet.
[05:17] Meera: that range is wide. if we have a $75k cap, how many tokens would that buy?
[05:22] Samira: rough calc: at $0.0005 per 1k tokens, $75k buys 150 billion tokens. but real effective tokens depend on caching, reorder and batching.
[05:33] Priya: about token-slicing — we heard Redwood supports token-slicing to reduce latency for long contexts. does that change cost calculations?
[05:41] Samira: token-slicing (sometimes called prefix-slicing) lets you stream partial context and only compute necessary segments; useful for long contexts where you can avoid re-evaluating the whole sequence. it can reduce latencies but sometimes increases total token compute if you recompute overlapping windows. you trade off total compute for latency.
[05:58] Daniel: so for our recommendation recall with long contexts, token-slicing might help latency during spikes but might increase monthly bill?
[06:04] Samira: exactly. we can test both modes in the pilot and give per-token and latency tradeoffs empirically.
[06:11] Alex: we also need SOC2 / KMS info for private options. can you share security docs?
[06:16] Jordan: yes — security pack link: https://redwood.example.com/security-pack (we'll send the specific SOC2/ISO attestations and KMS integration notes).
[06:24] Meera: for Private, how heavy is the deployment lift? we run EKS on-prem, not full air-gapped.
[06:30] Samira: Private has a control plane that can be customer-managed; typical install is a few weeks but depends on infra access. we support EKS and bare-metal. KMS/HSM integrations are supported — we'll share the runbook.
[06:42] Alex: curious about unit math for dedicated — we want an example for 16 GPU reservation.
[06:47] Samira: sure, rough example: say 16 A10 equivalent GPUs reserved; with efficient batching you might do X tokens/sec — okay ballpark numbers: 16 GPUs at 200k tokens/sec sustained is 17.28 billion tokens/day, but actual depends on model/seq len. amortize cost — if reservation is $Y/month, divide by tokens produced at target utilization. we'll run your real numbers in the spreadsheet.
[07:10] Priya: can you also show impact of increasing batch window from 20ms to 200ms? we worry about user-facing latency.
[07:16] Samira: yep, that's part of the bench. longer batch window increases throughput but hurts p50/p95. We'll produce curves.
[07:24] Jordan: quick note — competitors folks mentioned earlier? any names you care about?
[07:28] Alex: we looked at Anthropic and some self-hosted stacks — but integration overhead was big. we also benchmarked a managed provider but their SLA/visibility was lacking.
[07:37] Meera: one more compliance Q — audit logs and token retention. we need logs for 12 months and ability to purge.
[07:44] Jordan: Redwood logs are configurable and we can map retention to your policy; for Private you control logs fully. We'll include audit log notes in the security pack.
[07:55] Samira: ok, let's outline the pilot we propose: 2-week micro-benchmark (lab) + 4-week production pilot for a subset of traffic. deliverables: bench report, cost extrapolation, config recommendations (batching, cache, quantization), and routing policy.
[08:12] Priya: what's required from us to start?
[08:15] Samira: we need sample prompt sets, representative traffic traces (anonymized), target SLOs, and infra access for private tests. Also a small token budget for hosted test runs.
[08:25] Daniel: Daniel will send traces and our infra runbook.
[08:29] Alex: assume decision timelines — we want to decide by end of quarter.
[08:33] Jordan: that's reasonable. last piece: any hard blockers?
[08:36] Meera: KMS integration for PHI is a potential blocker if it takes long, also procurement will need detailed pricing.
[08:42] Jordan: we'll prioritize KMS notes in the security pack and get procurement a straightforward TCO spreadsheet.
[08:48] Samira: action items we'll list.
[08:52] [crosstalk] Priya: ok cool thanks everyone.

Note: transcription contains occasional mislabels (e.g., K V written out), filler words, and some partial overlaps.
action_items: Jordan: Send pricing spreadsheet and high-level TCO by 2026-09-04
Samira: Run lab micro-bench (assistant 7B latency, recall 33B throughput) and share results by 2026-09-09
Daniel: Provide anonymized traffic traces and infra runbook by 2026-09-05
Jordan: Share security pack (SOC2/KMS/HSM notes) and Private runbook links by 2026-09-03
next_steps: Schedule 30m bench kickoff next week (calendar invite from Jordan)
Samira to confirm exact instance types and test harness for bench
Customer to review pricing sheet and confirm pilot budget slice
